props.covers: The lab shell around the editing surface — the in-document page header, the fixed glass panel with its Edit/AI tabs, views, the annotation queue, autosave, and history.

text.insert: The editing surface is mounted inside a lab shell. The shell owns the document history, the save lifecycle, the annotation queue, and the panel. The surface owns only editing. The shell never fetches: persistence, manifest data, revision history, context previews, and the prompt-edit session all arrive as props or callbacks.
The document carries the agent's identity. A floating glass panel provides navigation and the AI workspace, with a compact rail as its resting state.
Layout

rows: Page header with title, model, description, and history inside the scroller, followed by the editing surface.
Persistent icon rail pinned at the top right. The compact outline and AI workspace expand to its left.
Style sidebar, owned by the host page.

text.insert: Each document scroller reserves 44px for the rail, plus the configured right inset and a 12px gap. The compact tree and AI workspace overlay the document without changing its width or line wrapping.
The Glass Panel

The panel starts as a collapsed icon rail. Selecting a view opens its compact tree while keeping the view controls at the right edge. The collapse control returns to the rail, and the AI control opens the annotation workspace.

rows: Expand, Prompt, Context, optional State and Tools, and AI.
Active view name and token count, host configuration and fixtures, collapsible outline, history, and selected-node details.
Annotation queue, or annotations pane for store-only hosts. The view rail remains available.

text.insert: The panel is anchored to the lab region's top-right corner using the configured insets. It expands left while the icon rail stays anchored. The content header and rail header share a 40px height, so their horizontal dividers align. Available region dimensions cap the panel's width and height.
Compact Tree Zones
The compact tree stacks host-fed zones under the view header, top to bottom. A zone renders only when its condition holds.

text.insert: Glass Treatment

The rail and expanded panel use the same translucent glass, subtle border, and shadow. The collapsed rail keeps its shadow so it reads as floating above the document. The background mixes 88% of the host glass color with transparency. Backdrop blur is 20px with saturation 1.3. Host glass, border, and shadow tokens remain authoritative.

The rail and panel body hide scrollbar tracks while retaining vertical scrolling when content exceeds the available height. Horizontal overflow is clipped. A full set of view controls fits the collapsed rail at its natural height without creating nested scrollbars.
Outline and History

The outline has no visible OUTLINE heading or dedicated action row. Its section adds 8px of top padding. The history icon floats at the section's top-right, with the same 8px top offset, and takes no space in document flow. It is positioned relative to the outline section, not fixed to the viewport. It appears only for the system view when the host supplies revisions.

Outline rows are 25px tall with 12px of indentation per depth level. Section labels jump to their document anchors, and separate chevrons fold child branches. One continuous hairline runs down the left edge of the list and jogs inward around the children of every expanded parent, so hierarchy is visible whether or not a branch is active. The active block, the current row's top-level section and its visible children, draws its part of that hairline in the selection accent. A dot on the line marks the current row. A folded parent that contains the current section takes the dot itself. Folded branches survive view and AI changes within the mounted lab.

The history control replaces the outline body with the host's revisions and toggles back to the tree. Its delayed tooltip reads History or Back to outline. Other host zones, including configuration, fixtures, and selected-node details, remain available.
Motion

Opening and closing preserve the document layout. Navigation content keeps its final width during the reveal, avoiding text rewrapping. The icon rail remains anchored through the transition. View changes use a short fade and vertical movement to soften the content replacement.

The accent segment and dot slide along the hairline, through the curves, rather than jumping between rows. Clicking a label pins the outline to that row for the whole smooth scroll. Scroll tracking resumes once the scroller has been quiet for 120ms, or immediately on a scroll-end event. Folding or unfolding a branch changes the hairline's shape, so the accent and dot snap to their new positions instead of animating across the list.

rows: Opacity fades in as the glass opens.
Opacity fades out before visibility becomes hidden.
Opacity moves from 0 to 1 while translateY moves from 6px to 0, using the same easing as the panel.

The accent segment and dot slide along the hairline with cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1), an ease-out with no overshoot, measured from the Mintlify table of contents. The active label's color fades over the same duration.

text.insert: Reduced-motion preferences disable panel transitions, view-entry animations, and the outline's sliding accent, dot, and label fade. Initial mounting does not play the view-switch animation. Collapsed content is hidden from accessibility navigation and made inert immediately, while its visual fade completes. Focus inside content that closes returns to the rail toggle.
Views

Prompt selects the system editing view. Context shows the assembled context as a read-only document. State and Tools appear when the host supplies their zones. State shows the selected fixture, and Tools shows the rendered tool definitions. Undo, redo, and save operate only in the system view. Selecting any view icon opens its compact tree.
The lab has no Raw or Sections view. The Prompt view already shows the XML-tagged Markdown the agent receives. Block editing works on that view rather than on an alternative document.
Icons and Labels

rows: Instructions. The panel heading and button name use Prompt; the tooltip and URL use System and system.
Annotation workspace. Tooltip: AI workspace, or Return to navigation when active.

text.insert: The open book avoids the copy-action meaning of overlapping pages. Curly braces distinguish state data from settings sliders. Icons render at 16px inside 32px controls, with an active tint and visible keyboard-focus ring. AI displays a busy indicator only while work is running.
Tooltips

Tooltips contain only the short label. They have no description, token count, or save-status sentence. Hover and keyboard focus open them after 400ms. Leaving before the delay cancels opening. Pointer exit allows a 100ms grace period to enter the tooltip. Click, blur, scrolling, or resize dismisses a visible tooltip.

Tooltips float outside the glass clipping boundary, beside their controls. They use compact dark styling, 12px text, and 5px vertical by 8px horizontal padding. A visible tooltip is linked to its button through
aria-describedby
. Escape dismisses it before the lab handles that key. The active view's token count stays in the panel header.
Host Navigation
The host can control selection through
view
and
onViewChange
. Observatory stores the view in
/:projectId/agent/:agentName/:view
and shows Project / Agent / View in its page header. The route accepts
system
context
state
, and
tools
. Missing or unrecognized view segments select
system
. Reload, Back, and Forward restore the selected view. Rail expansion and folded branches are local UI state and are not encoded in that URL.

AI annotations target the system prompt. Opening AI from another view switches to system and remembers the previous view. Returning restores that view and the prior collapsed or expanded navigation state. Selecting a view icon from AI opens that view's tree. Host navigation away from system clears AI mode so browser history cannot restore stale annotation mode.
The Annotation Queue
Everything queues. Nothing runs until Apply.
The inline composer (Cursor-style single box, ring-aligned above the pinned
target) files on Enter: node targets as
batch
, document targets as
global
. An open composer is sticky, only its × or Escape closes it.
The AI tab's queue panel is a chat layout: TARGETS section (rows: violet

human-readable target label, the note indented beneath, quiet state, × on
  hover), DOCUMENT section (whole-document notes plus their own input), slim
  ✓/✕ records with Undo, and a bottom dock holding the one click-only Apply.
Apply opens ONE session over the whole queue in filing order. The agent

surveys every request before editing, then stages one proposal per request:
  n reviewable diffs forming an ordered stack (accept from the head, reject
  from the tail, with per-action disabled reasons).
Comment presence renders only in the AI state: margin count bubbles, a thin

violet tick down commented rows, and a hover wash linking queue row to target block. Clicking a bubble reopens the inline composer prefilled with the note. Saving refiles (same target and disposition, fresh id) and dismisses the original.
Row states speak only when meaningful:
processing
(breathing dot, violet
bar),
staged
(green),
waiting on you

(amber, with the inline reply).
  Positions and counts are not rendered, order is the list order.
History
The shell's history wraps the transaction log with one interface:

Two edit channels share one undo stack. Block edits arrive as steps and go to the inner transaction log. Document-metadata edits, title and description, live in an overlay with their own before/after entries. The unified stack interleaves both kinds. Marking a save moves only the dirty baseline, so undo keeps working across a save. Dirtiness compares the canonical serialization of the current document against the saved canonical string. The inner log's content hash is a cheap local prefix. Authoritative hashes come from the save API.
Autosave

Autosave is a generic debounced-save coordinator: 1500ms debounce,
single-flight with a trailing save, newest-value-wins, cancelled whenever the
draft is clean or carries validation errors, Cmd+S flushes.

Healthy autosave is silent. An attention dot on the Prompt icon exposes saving, unsaved changes, validation errors, or save failures while the rail is collapsed. Exceptional save status and retry controls appear above the expanded navigation content and in the AI workspace. Save errors also render under the document header.
Shortcuts

Cmd+Z, Cmd+Shift+Z, and Cmd+S bind on the document, guarded to events inside the lab or with nothing focused. Escape dismisses a visible tooltip first. Otherwise it closes an open annotation composer, returns from AI, or collapses an expanded tree in that order. Events already handled by a child are respected. Undo and redo use keyboard shortcuts.
External Saves

An MCP edit updates the canonical prompt independently of an unsaved browser draft. Host saves use the shared revision-checked store: an outdated browser hash conflicts instead of overwriting the external change. Reload and reconcile before resubmitting. Local editor undo and durable external change undo have distinct histories.
